name: Antique Pink
lede: Antique Pink is a dusty, warm pink standardized by the German RAL system as RAL 3014, and recorded six years earlier by Maerz and Paul under a different name entirely.

sections.title: A name in the library
sections.body:
The German RAL color-matching system, in use since 1927, lists this shade as RAL 3014 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately dates the same hue to 1926, plate 3, swatch I 2, under the name "Vassar Roset" [1]. Two dictionaries, two different names, for what the library computes as the same color [1].

The nearest color-graph neighbors are [[candy-pink]] and [[dirty-pink]], tied at 3.0 units away, with [[light-jasper-red]] and [[dusty-rose]] close behind, and [[new-york-pink]] and [[pink-coral]] a touch further at 4.6 and 4.7 [2]. Munsell gives 2.8R 5.9/8.9, a medium-lightness, moderately saturated red-pink [1]. The hex #D47479 is a screen approximation of the RAL chip, which is itself a physical paint sample, not a dye [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pink in 9 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.04 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is a 1400 Italian panel, *A Bishop Saint with a Donor*, from the Cleveland Museum, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. Later matches cluster in early modernist portraits and florals: Henri Matisse's *Nude with a White Scarf* (1909), Ernst Ludwig Kirchner's *Two Girls under an Umbrella* (1910), and Lovis Corinth's *Iris und Päonien* (1911) [3]. Chinese and German paintings both show a notably higher rate of this pink than the archive average, though the counts are small [3].

What name did Maerz and Paul give this same color in 1926?
